Secondly, my delegation would also like to highlight the importance of the report adopted by the Group of Governmental Experts on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems at the end of the last session last week. In the adverse multilateral context, that the group had fulfilled its mandate and arrived by consensus to a substantive output is an achievement worthy of being recognized as such. which is why I would like to extend my most sincere congratulations to Ambassador Robert Inderhandt for the exemplary way in which he led the group during his entire mandate, and for the patience, the transparency, and the negotiating acumen with which he led these discussions up until their conclusion. Argentina reiterates that the CCW is the right forum to give this debate further life. The work built by the Group over the years, and particularly the report adopted last week, are an excellent foundation upon which we can project future work. But my delegation wishes to be clear: it is necessary to raise the admission level. The Seventh Review Conference must agree on a mandate that is guided towards adopting an instrument that will lay down clear rules and specific measures on how to regulate this area. And we trust that this preparatory committee will know how to lay down the foundation to go down that path. We would like to thank Ambassador Salcedo and Peru in this regard for having chosen to guide our work for the Second Committee, and we pledge our delegation's full support. Thank you very much, Mr. President.
I would like to thank the distinguished delegate of Argentina for his statement and recognize Brazil. Distinguished Representative Yaloffor.

Mr. President-designate, my delegation congratulates you, Ambassador Giuliantoni, for your appointment as President-designate of the Seventh Review Conference of the CCW. We trust that under your able and wise leadership, the Conference will achieve a successful and meaningful outcome. and we are encouraged by the competent and determined efforts you have already undertaken to ensure that goal. Brazil reaffirms its strong commitment to the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons and its annexed protocols as essential instruments of international humanitarian law. This conference provides an opportunity not only to reaffirm the enduring principles and objectives of the Convention, but also to equip it to respond effectively to the challenges of the coming review cycle. Brazil attaches particular importance to a substantive, balanced, and forward-looking outcome of the seventh review conference. Brazil supports a final outcome that reaffirms the central role of the CCW as an instrument of international humanitarian law, strengthens universalization, national implementation, and compliance, promotes international cooperation and assistance, and preserves the Convention's capacity to respond to developments in weapons, means, and methods of warfare. We believe that the final documents should translate our deliberations into concrete action. In this regard, we welcome the fact that the Group of Governmental Experts on Lethal Autonomous Weapon Systems successfully fulfilled its mandate, adopting a substantive report that contains a set of elements of an instrument on this issue. We appreciate and commend the efforts of the Chairman of the GGE LOS, Ambassador Robert van den Bos. While the report has important shortcomings, it provides a solid foundation for our future efforts on this issue, and in particular, for negotiations of an instrument on LOS. During the last session of the GGE, Brazil delivered a statement on behalf of 47 states, co-drafted with Ireland and Norway, in which the aspiration of using the results of the GGE as a basis for negotiations in the CCW was clearly expressed. We cannot let that call be unanswered. Brazil firmly believes that the Review Conference should take a meaningful step forward and provide a mandate for such negotiations to start, using the GGE report as its basis. Our strong preference is that such negotiations lead to the adoption of a legally binding instrument in the form of a new protocol to the CCW. Mr. President-designate, After several years in which procedural issues have constrained substantive discussions, this review conference offers an opportunity to restore the Convention to its full and effective functioning. Brazil stands ready to engage constructively with all high contracting parties towards this objective. Regarding the negotiations on the final documents, Brazil believes we should seek an outcome capable of commanding the broadest possible support while ensuring that our working methods enable, rather than prevent, the Convention from fulfilling its humanitarian purpose. Our objective should not be merely to preserve the CCW, but to strengthen its relevance, effectiveness and capacity to respond to contemporary realities. Brazil stands ready to contribute to that objective. Thank you, Mr. President.
I would like to thank the distinguished representative of Brazil for his statement and now recognize the distinguished representative of Mexico. You have the floor.

Muchas gracias.

Thank you very much, Mr. President. I would like to begin by congratulating you on your election to preside over our work. You can count on the full support and constructive contributions of the Mexican delegation as we crown this preparatory session with success. Mexico reiterates a strong commitment to the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, as well as the principles and standards of international humanitarian law. From our perspective, continues to be a fundamental instrument to reduce human suffering arising from the use of certain conventional weapons, as well as to improve protection of civilian populations and all those affected by armed conflict. The CCW is, further, an opportunity that we should fully leverage in order to move forward in the disarmament objectives as well as in strengthening and developing international humanitarian law. Which is why Mexico believes that it is indispensable to preserve and strengthen the dynamic nature of the CCW. The convention ought to maintain its responsibility to effectively address the changes and methods and means of war, the fast technological developments, and the transformations in which hostilities are carried out. Mexico will continue to support the progressive development of international law when necessary to prevent and reduce the humanitarian consequences arising from the use of excessively harmful weapons or indiscriminate effects, as well as to preserve and strengthen the integrity of international humanitarian law. Mr. President, This matter becomes particularly important given the developments related to the autonomous weapons systems. Mexico wishes to recognize the very arduous work and the commitment of all delegations that participated in the Group of Government Experts on Autonomous Weapons Systems, whose work concluded last Friday. We also recognize the leadership and the efforts of Ambassador Robert Inderbosch of the Netherlands conducting this group, as well as his efforts to facilitate dialogue and to find common ground on a particularly complicated matter. The work done ought to allow us to continue to move forward using a different modality. Mexico is willing to work with all delegations in order to build upon the foundation of the progress made and the various perspectives shared during this process. Here, an international, clear, effective, and legally binding framework that sets forth prohibitions and regulations that can be applied to autonomous weapons systems. For Mexico, the human element must remain at the core of this effort. to preserve human judgment and control is essential, not just to guarantee that international maritime law is enforced and respected, but also to guarantee responsibility and accountability. With a view to the seventh review conference, Mexico will be constructively participating with the expectation that we will be able to attain substantive results that will strengthen the convention and its ability to address both current challenges and those that are emerging. The Review Conference is an opportunity which we should take full advantage of in order to revitalize the work of the CCW. This means that we need output that reflects contemporary humanitarian concerns and that allows us to move forward in areas in which there is room for improvement of norms, procedures and mechanisms of the Convention. For Mexico, the effectiveness of this system does not depend solely on the robustness of its legal instruments. It also hinges on the political will of states to fully meet their obligations, to preserve the humanitarian purpose of the convention, and to guarantee that it continues to address the realities of armed conflict. It is important to show that this framework is able to evolve when circumstances and the protection of individuals so require it. The work of these three days ought to lay down a foundation to attain that goal.

Thank you very much.

I thank the representative of Mexico for her statement. And now I would like to give the floor to the following delegations, Sweden, the Republic of Korea, and the Philippines. Sweden, you have the floor. Distinguished representative of Sweden.

Mr. President, let me begin by congratulating you on your appointment as president of the upcoming review conference. I can assure you of the full support from the Swedish delegation. Sweden fully aligns itself with the statement to be delivered by the European Union. I wish to add the following remarks in a national capacity. Mr. President, Sweden remains committed to the CCW and its protocols. We believe in the Convention's capacity to balance security needs and humanitarian concerns. We urge all States who have not joined the Convention or its protocols to do so without further delay. Sweden believes that the CCW and its protocols remain effective and relevant instruments for addressing both current and future developments in weapons technology. In this regard, Sweden welcomes the successful conclusion of the work of the GGE LOS and the consensus outcome achieved. This is an accomplishment that demonstrates that CCW remains a relevant and effective forum for addressing emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapons systems. We especially commend the GGE Chair, Ambassador Innamboch, and his team for their tireless efforts to reach an agreement, as well as all delegations for their constructive engagement. And we look forward to build on this achievement at the seventh review conference. Mr. President, we would like to reiterate the importance of ensuring the Convention's financial stability. Important measures were agreed during the Sixth Review Conference, and we look forward to their full implementation. The sustainability and effective functioning of the Convention require the full and timely payment of assessed contributions by all High Contracting Parties. Furthermore, Sweden remains firmly committed to advancing gender equality. We are convinced that the systematic integration of a gender perspective across arms control, disarmament and non-proliferation processes strengthens both the effectiveness and inclusiveness of our collective efforts. Let me also underline the importance we attach to the participation of civil society organizations and their valuable contributions to the CCW and our continued work. Thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Sweden for that statement. And now I give the floor to the Ambassador of South Korea. You have the floor.

Mr. President, at outset, I'd like to congratulate you on the assumption of the presidency of the seventh review conference of the CCW. My delegation has full confidence in your able leadership. in guiding this preparatory committee and upcoming review conference to a successful outcome. I'd like to assure you my delegation's continued support in your endeavors. The Republic of Korea reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the CCW, which plays an indispensable role in balancing security and humanitarian considerations in armed conflict. Korea remains fully committed to fulfilling its obligations under the convention and its protocol, including through the regular submission of national report. We welcome and appreciate the effort undertaken by the President to promote wider adherence to the Convention. The universalization still remains an important unfinished task. We therefore encourage states that have not yet acceded to the Convention to do so at the earliest opportunity. Mr. President, we commend the work of the coordinators for Amended Protocol II and Protocol V, including the work on improvised explosive devices, as we share grave concern regarding the devastating effects of such weapons on civilians. However, my delegation deeply regrets that in recent years, the meetings of the High Contracting Parties and annual conferences on AP II and Protocol V have fallen short of their purpose. These annual meetings serve as vital platforms for the exchange of views and for further strengthening the CCW framework. We sincerely hope that the current political impasse can be overcome at the upcoming review conference, restoring the full functioning of these annual meetings. We would also like to highlight the important contributions of observers, including intergovernmental organizations, the ICRC, and civil society, to the work of the Convention. The Republic of Korea supports the full participation of all observers. Mr. President, a unique strength of the CCW is its flexibility to adapt to an evolving security landscape. In this regard, the Group of Governmental Experts on Lethal Autonomous Weapon Systems provides an important forum for High Contracting Parties to address emerging technologies that may shape the nature of armed conflict in the future. My delegation welcomes the adoption of the final report of the Group, which culminates three years of intensive and substantive discussions. The elements adopted by consensus represent a remarkable milestone in the history of the CCW and the broader disarmament community. This outcome demonstrates that our community can make meaningful progress in addressing emerging challenges despite geopolitical tensions. We look forward to constructive deliberations on how to carry this important work forward at the review conference. My delegation wishes to express its sincere appreciation to the chair of the group, Ambassador Robert Inden Bosch of the Netherlands, for his able leadership. The consensus report would not have been possible without his meticulous, tireless, and tenacious work. We also commend Team Netherlands and ISU for its important contribution to this outcome. We will make a more detailed statement regarding the future mandate of the GGE during our discussion under Main Committee II. At this stage, we would like to highlight our view that the GGE is the most appropriate forum and the future discussion on laws should continue to take place within the CCW framework. Mr. President, to continue our crucial work within the CCW framework, is vital to maintain the Convention's financial integrity and sustainability. Alongside the implementation of consolidated financial measures adopted at the sixth review conference to the full and timely payment of assessed contributions by all high contracting parties would be essential to strengthening the CCW's financial standing and ensuring the effective functioning of its mechanisms. To conclude, The CCW is the cornerstone of the rules-based international order and multilateralism that has contributed to international peace and security for decades. I sincerely hope that our collective wisdom can find a way forward based upon the common ground we have already found. Thank you.
I thank the ambassador. of the Republic of Korea for his statement. And now I give the floor to the Philippines.

Thank you, Mr. President. The Philippines would like to congratulate you, Ambassador Tony, for taking on the role of leading the seventh review conference of the CCW. We are confident in your ability to steer the conference in an effective and substantive manner. The Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons is an important tenet of humanitarian disarmament. The Philippines' commitment to this convention is firmly anchored on our constitutional renunciation of war as an instrument of policy and our unwavering commitment to international humanitarian law. This review conference comes at a critical juncture. The global security landscape faces multiple armed conflicts, increasingly sophisticated warfare, and an erosion of multilateralism. As these conflicts intensify, the core principles of humanitarian disarmament are increasingly put to the test. Against this backdrop, we urge substantive discussions that prioritize the voices of communities directly impacted by conventional weapons. In our region, improvised explosive devices and explosive remnants of war continue to threaten livelihoods, safety, and human security. Meaningful exchange is therefore vital to our delegation. To achieve this, we urge the efficient and structured use of our time to address all essential facets of the Convention. Mr. President, with the conclusion of the mandate of the Group of Governmental Experts on Lethal Autonomous Weapon Systems, we look forward to the conference deciding on a forward-looking mandate to govern these existing technologies. Establishing a negotiating mandate for a legally binding instrument and laws represents the necessary next step for high contracting parties. Furthermore, we recommend that adequate time be allocated to thoroughly review and finalize the draft report of the review conference. Given the ongoing use of weapons that violate IHL across current conflict zones, the Philippines hopes the outcome of this conference will provide clear, actionable momentum for the regime. On administrative matters, we call for the transparent management of the Convention's financial resources. The Philippines remains fully committed to fulfilling its assessed contributions in a complete and timely manner. Transparent financial stewardship is an obligation we owe to the constituents we serve. Our delegation stands ready to engage constructively and fully supports your leadership, Mr. President, in guiding us toward a successful outcome.

Thank you.

I thank the distinguished representative of the Philippines for her statement. And now I give the floor to the following delegations. They're the last on my list. So we may be able to conclude with the segment devoted to the statements. Israel, Cuba, Ireland, and South Africa. I give the floor now to the distinguished representative of Israel.

And good morning, colleagues. Mr. Chair, at the outset, allow me to congratulate you, Ambassador, for your election as President-designate on the seventh review conference of the CCW, and to express our delegation's full cooperation and support in the discharge of your duties. We wish to thank the ISU members for the intensive efforts in preparation for this meeting and for the upcoming meeting in November. Mr. President, Israel attaches great importance to the CCW and its commitment and ability to strike the appropriate balance between military and humanitarian considerations. Now, more than ever before, the importance of our work here is demonstrated in its clearest form. We convene this meeting in the midst of troubling geopolitical times. The international community is unprecedentedly challenged by the malicious behavior of rogue states and terrorist groups who serve as their proxies. Mr. President, international law was developed in order to try to minimize the terrible consequences of war. It is the international community's collective responsibility to address the abuse of international law by terrorist organizations, also in the context of using conventional weapons. Mr. Chair, allow me to take the opportunity to congratulate and express our gratitude to the Ambassador of the Netherlands, His Excellency Mr. Robert Inderbosch, and his team for his skillful leadership of the GGE on Laws, which has allowed us to reach a significant milestone in this highly important topic. This achievement by the GGE is the most recent example of why the CCW is the most appropriate forum to continue our discussion on the topic. The final report is a result of multilateral discussions conducted under a clear mandate that has brought us to an outcome that indeed does not prejudge the nature of our agreed recommendations and possible elements, and it should be viewed as such. We stand ready to continue the constructive discussion in a future mandate as determined by the CCW High Contracting Parties in November. Mr. President, we look forward to engage constructively with the important work of this body. We wish you, your team, and all participants a successful meeting.

Thank you.

I thank the distinguished representative of Israel. And now I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Cuba.

Thank you very much, Chair. My delegation would like to thank you for this opportunity to take the floor during this preparatory meeting to the seventh review conference of the CCW. We congratulate you on your nomination as the chair of this conference. Cuba as a party to the convention to also AP2 original and other protocols remains fully committed to this instrument. The full compliance with these documents will ensure the right balance with the legitimate defense of our territory and will not affect the purely defensive nature of our defenses. So any questions related to full compliance with the original protocol two is no longer valid. A treaty can only be distinguished on the basis of agreement by all countries. Cuba respects the sovereign decisions of countries to adhere to AP2, but we remain committed to the original instruments. Any attempts to force us to change this position will be an error. On the question of laws, Cuba remained loyal to its position that IHL fully applies to these systems, but that is not enough and does not ensure meaningful human control over these weapons. We need additional legal measures. An algorithm cannot replace the ethical judgment and the obligations of states and individuals under IHL. After a decade of discussions, The GG achieved a very valuable result, but it's not sufficient in the face of this challenge. The review conference should be a turning point in this respect. We urge countries to strengthen the mandate of the group with a focus on specific results and to start without any delay negotiations on a legally binding instrument that will ban laws and regulate semi-autonomous weapon systems. in line with IHL and human rights law. This position is fully in compliance with the position of Cuba, shown in our support to the relevant resolutions on laws. We must achieve a legally binding framework on these issues. The CCW is the appropriate forum to move forward on these questions, and we hope that the review conference will reflect in its results both priorities. Thank you.

Thank you very much to the distinguished representative of Cuba. And now I'd like to give the floor to Ireland, to be followed by South Africa and then Spain. I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Ireland.

Thank you, President-designate. Ireland aligns itself with the statement by the European Union and wishes to add the following remarks in a national capacity. At the outset, please allow me to congratulate you on your appointment as President-designate of the Seventh Review Conference and to assure you of my delegation's full support. Ireland is committed to supporting the universalization of the Convention and the implementation of its protocols. We firmly believe that the Convention and its protocols represent a crucial instrument of international humanitarian law and a vital tool to further the protection of civilians, combatants and peacekeepers during and after conflict. We reiterate Ireland's strong support for inclusive participation in this forum, including the meaningful engagement of civil society and gender-responsive approaches to disarmament. Ireland has a number of priorities for the upcoming Seventh Review Conference, the first being with regard to addressing the urgent challenges posed by autonomous weapons systems. We commend the work of Ambassador Robert In 't Veld of the Kingdom of the Netherlands for the impressive efforts of him and his team, as well as the ISU, that led to consensus adoption of a substantive outcome document late last week. While the final product may not have been as ambitious as we and other delegations may have wished for, it is a welcome sign of progress particularly on characterizing laws and further defining the human element needed for compliance with international law and armed conflict. We need to build on such momentum. In this vein, we wish to see advancement of negotiations within the CCW on an instrument on lethal autonomous weapon systems at the forthcoming seventh review conference. This call echoes the widespread urgency voiced around the world to move forward, including at last week's final GGE session, through the joint statement delivered by Algeria on behalf of the African states, high contracting parties to the CCW, and likewise the joint statement delivered by Brazil, coordinated together with Norway and Ireland on behalf of 47 states, which called on using the outcome of the GGE as a basis for future negotiations. After over 10 years of discussions and with concerning reports of the use of these systems in contemporary conflicts around the world, negotiations are overdue. We have more than enough material and common understandings to begin negotiations in which outstanding issues can and should be discussed. President, mines other than anti-personnel mines remain an issue of humanitarian urgency. Ireland reiterates that expert discussions within the CCW on this issue would benefit all and contribute to reduced humanitarian harm. President, I conclude by conveying Ireland's deep concern over reported use of incendiary weapons and weapons with incendiary effects in Ukraine, Gaza, Lebanon and Syria. We reiterate that all parties must strictly comply with IHL, including the general prohibition for weapons, means or methods of warfare with indiscriminate effects. In light of the severe humanitarian concerns around the use of incendiary weapons and uses of weapons with incidental incendiary effects, We reiterate that it is overdue for the CCW to return to meaningfully discussing the implementation of Protocol III, as well as to consider measures to bolster its universalisation. President, Ireland is determined to ensure that the CCW fulfils its role in strengthening international humanitarian law as the means and methods of warfare rapidly develop, posing new and complex challenges. We will play our part in ensuring a successful seventh review conference in November, the response to these challenges and strengthens its humanitarian objectives. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Ireland. And now I give the floor to the distinguished representative of South Africa. You have the floor.

At the outset, South Africa wishes to congratulate you on your appointment as the President-designate. of the Seventh Review Conference. You can count on South Africa's full support throughout this process. South Africa aligns itself with the objectives and provisions of the CCW and its annex protocols, to all of which South Africa is a high contracting party. The convention remains a cornerstone of international humanitarian law and has, for more than four decades, provided an important framework for addressing the humanitarian impact of certain conventional weapons while balancing military necessity with humanitarian considerations. My delegation wishes to commend Ambassador Robert Indenbosch and his team for the outstanding leadership in steering the work of the GGE on laws. Under his stewardship, the group successfully navigated a challenging international environment and achieved consensus on a substantive report, thereby fulfilling a mandate entrusted to it by high contracting parties. At the same time, when geopolitical tensions continue to affect many regions of the world, this achievement demonstrates the enduring value of multilateralism, dialogue and compromise. Mr. President, building on this progress, South Africa attaches great importance to the future mandate on laws. Our delegation believes that the momentum generated by the GGE must be preserved and that discussions should continue in a structured manner until agreement is reached on a negotiating mandate on an instrument. We remain convinced that the CCW provides the most suitable forum for these deliberations and express the hope that we will see even stronger participation from African High Contracting Parties in future discussions on this important issue. While emerging technologies remain an important area of focus, South Africa also believes that there is merit in broadening our discussions within the CCW to reflect on the continued relevance, implementation and global impact of the Convention and its annexed protocols. The CCW framework has made a significant contribution to strengthening respect for international humanitarian law, reducing human suffering and enhancing civilian protection in armed conflict. A comprehensive reflection on how the Convention and its annex protocols continue to respond to contemporary security and humanitarian challenges would be both timely and valuable. South Africa further wishes to express its appreciation to the ISU for its support to high contracting parties. We acknowledge that the importance of the role played by the sponsorship program in promoting universalization and facilitating broader participation in the work of the Convention. As preparations for the seventh review conference continue, South Africa looks forward to engaging constructively with all high contracting parties to strengthen the Convention and advance its implementation and ensure that it remains responsive to the current and future humanitarian challenges.
I thank the distinguished representative of South Africa and I give the floor to the Ambassador of Spain. You have the floor, Madam.

Thank you very much, Chair. At the outset, I would like to align myself with the statement that will be made by the European Union later during this general debate. Just like other colleagues, I would like to start by thanking you and by congratulating you on having accepted the chairmanship of the seventh review conference of the CCW. Spain has been a high contracting party to this convention and we are really committed with all of the articles and the work carried out. This convention is a cornerstone of international humanitarian law. And what we'd like to see is that all High Contracting Parties, the Secretariat and yourself can in the upcoming weeks and months to take additional steps that we find really necessary to contribute to the universalization of the Convention. And just like other States that mentioned this before, me, Spain gives special importance to the contributions made by civil society, the ICRC and other international organizations, the contributions to the work that we carry out here as we prepare for the Seventh Review Conference and also during the Review Conference. So we're looking forward to their contributions. Just like other colleagues, we would also like to highlight and thank Ambassador of the Netherlands, Robert 'm den Bosch, and thank his team and the secretariat for the work carried out last week in the GGE on laws, an extremely important forum, and the work that was carried out, as well as the approval on the basis of consensus of the elements. Elements that were approved last Friday are absolutely crucial for us and for the future work on this issue. And we believe, just like others who spoke before me, the success of the work of the GGE on laws is the success of the presidency, the chair, but also of all of us. And this is yet another demonstration of support to multilateralism. And this was a multilateral forum where we've seen the political will of everybody. And we achieved results last week. So we do hope that this is an area where we can make progress in the future under the CCW. And it is indeed the platform where we should continue our work in the upcoming weeks and months. And finally, Chair, in connection with the seventh review conference for Spain, it is important to ensure that the conference Just like this preparatory committee work that helps us prepare the work that we'll be carrying out in November, we need to ensure that it is a conference of substance where decisions can be taken, substantive decisions. And for that, you can count on the constructive work of my delegation We will participate constructively in the entire review conference. So we wish you good luck as you carry out your mission.

Thank you.

I thank the Ambassador of Spain for her statement. And with this, we have concluded the statements of high contracting parties. I see that Norway would like to take the floor. Please, I invite the distinguished representative of Norway.

Thank you, President Teich, for giving me the floor. First, congratulations on your nomination, and thank you for the work that you, your team, and the ISU have undertaken in the preparation of the Seventh Review Conference. The CCW remains an important instrument for addressing the humanitarian and security implications of conventional weapons and emerging technologies. At the same time, the protection of civilians and the strengthening of international humanitarian law rely on a broader framework of treaties, norms and political commitments. Instruments such as the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention, the Cluster Munitions Convention and the Political Declaration on Explosive Weapons in Populated Areas complement the work undertaken under CCW and contribute to reducing human suffering caused by armed conflict. Across the world, civilians continue to live with the effects of mines, explosive remnants of war and other conventional weapons that kill, injure and constrain lives long after conflicts have ended. Addressing these human costs and strengthening the protection afforded by international humanitarian law should remain at the heart of our deliberations. President-designate. Not only is the CCW a central body of international law itself, providing layers of humanitarian protection, it has repeatedly proven to be an important venue for states and experts to come together to discuss and address emerging humanitarian challenges and concerns related to weapons, means and methods of warfare. The CCW is a dynamic instrument. It gives us a tool to tackle new developments. It has been an incubator for the emergence of new important norms. Norway aims to use this RevCon to advance universalization of our Convention, to assess implementation and compliance to date, devise new means to strengthen implementation, as well as to provide an action-oriented agenda for work in the years to come. I would like to highlight the following issues. First, we need to establish a framework for sustained and regular attention to Protocol III, like we have for Protocols II and V. Second, mines other than anti-personnel mines have significant humanitarian impact. We aim for this Review Conference to set up a framework for sustained attention to this issue. Third, The GGE on LAWS successful conclusion of a substantive report containing elements of an instrument on lethal autonomous weapons systems provides us with the basis that we finally need to begin negotiations on an instrument on LAWS within the CCW. While the final report had clear shortcomings, we believe that it provides us with a sufficient basis to start negotiations in which all outstanding questions can and will be addressed. Our priority for this RevCon is to establish a mandate for such negotiations, as called for in two widely supported joint statements the last week. Fourth, the CCW has been mired in procedural issues in this past review cycle. We do not want to see a repetition of last year's meeting of High Contracting Parties without substantive work. This review conference is our opportunity to address these issues decisively, to ensure the full and effective functioning of our machineries in the years to come. President-designate, we also underline the importance of ensuring broad and meaningful participation in the work of the Convention. International organizations, the ICRC, civil society and other observers bring expertise and perspective that strengthen our deliberations and contribute to better informed outcomes. Their participation should be free from undue subjective constraints from the side of the High Contracting Parties. President-designate. Norway looks forward to working constructively with all delegations in the preparations ahead.

Thank you.

I thank the distinguished representative of Norway. And now we will turn to observers. On the list, I apologize, says the Chair, I see the distinguished representative of Bangladesh. You have the floor.

Thank you, Mr. Chair, for your nomination. We remain at your disposal in living up to the mandate given by this body. Bangladesh attaches great importance to the seventh review conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, to be held in November this year. The review conference provides an important opportunity to reaffirm the continued relevance of the convention as a key framework for addressing the humanitarian consequences of emerging weapons technologies. It promises to strengthen its effectiveness and ensuring that it remains responsive to evolving technological developments. From Bangladesh's perspective, the CCW's consensus-based approach remains particularly valuable. Strengthening the convention requires preserving its humanitarian purpose ensuring the effective implementation of its existing provisions. In this context, Bangladesh recognizes the important contribution of the group of governmental experts on emerging technologies in the area of laws. The GGE's mandate to consider and formulate by consensus elements of an instrument without prejudicing its legal nature provides a critical avenue for developing common understandings and practical measures on laws. The recent progress and consensus achieved in identifying elements for a future instrument represent an important foundation for further work. We are grateful to the leadership of the Netherlands and Ambassador Bos for his very painstaking job over the years. Bangladesh believes that the outcome of the GGS work should be carried forward with ambition and translated into meaningful decisions at the review conference. The seventh review conference should therefore provide clear political direction towards the commencement of negotiations on an effective international instrument to regulate laws. It is very urgent to ensure that States and human beings remain responsible and accountable for decisions concerning the use of force. Bangladesh stands ready to engage constructively with all States to strengthen the CCW and advance a balanced, inclusive and humanitarian response to the challenges posed by lethal autonomous weapons systems. Thank you, Mr. Chair.

I thank the distinguished representative of Bangladesh. Now I'd like to give the floor to observers. On my list, I have the delegation of the European Union, then International Humanitarian Law Youth Initiative, and Institute for Global Negotiations. The European Union, you have the floor.

Thank you, Mr. President-designate. I have the honor to speak on behalf of the European Union and its member states. At the outset, the EU wishes to convey its deep appreciation for all your efforts in paving the way for a successful and substantive outcome of the seventh review conference. We pledge our full cooperation and support for achieving an ambitious outcome and a solid plan for future work during the next review cycle. This will require common efforts of all high contracting parties. The EU recalls that the CCW and its protocols are key instruments for an integral part of an international humanitarian law and reiterates its commitments of the EU and its member states respecting and fully complying with IHL, as well as to continue to adhere fully to the EU guidelines on the promotion of compliance with IHL. We underline that CCW is a unique international forum gathering diplomatic, legal, and military expertise and an appropriate forum to respond to fast-paced developments in the field of weapons technology, thus, by its mandate, contributing to preventing and reducing the suffering of both civilians and combatants. Ensuring that the effectiveness of the convention in the future is preserved and that it further strengthened including by keeping the Convention responsive to new developments and emerging technologies, should be a priority for the review conference. The EU emphasizes the importance of the universalization of the Convention and its protocols and recalls the EU efforts in this regard. In view of enhancing the strength and effectiveness of the Convention and its protocols, we encourage all States that have not yet done so to join the CCW and its protocols without further delay. We stress the importance of inclusive CCW discussions with the active participation of all stakeholders and the technical expertise by observers playing a pivotal role in broadening the scope of CCW debate and ensuring a comprehensive understanding of the complex issues under consideration. Young people have closely followed these discussions within the GGE on laws and have contributed our perspectives on international humanitarian law, human control, human responsibility, and the humanitarian ethical risk associated with autonomy in weapons. We therefore look for the seventh review conference to establish clear and effective prohibitions and restrictions on lethal autonomous weapons systems. We do not want future generations to live in a world where responsibility for lethal force becomes divided between the developer, the operator and the system itself, leaving no one clearly accountable for the outcome.
